finding.claim: Formula dependency chains recurse without a depth limit: cellResolver calls calcCellValue again, so a long acyclic chain of formula cells can exhaust the goroutine stack and abort the process with an unrecoverable fatal error.
finding.source: The <f> text of a sequence of formula cells in an attacker-supplied sheet (each referencing the next).
finding.sink: Recursive call cellResolver -> calcCellValue at calc.go:1827, via evalInfixExp at calc.go:961.

trace.note: formulaArgCache checked; only populated after return, so no short-circuit on first traversal
MaxCalcIterations check only limits revisits of the same ref (cycles)
recursive calcCellValue with no depth counter

finding.guards_checked: MaxCalcIterations only bounds revisits of one cell, which handles cycles but not long acyclic chains. formulaArgCache is only written after the recursive call returns. No depth limit exists in the formula engine (grep for depth/recursion limits found none). Impact unverified: stack cost per level not measured, so the required chain length is unknown.

finding.claim: The default UnzipSizeLimit of about 16.9GB allows a roughly 17MB xlsx to expand fully into memory: non-worksheet parts are preallocated to their declared size and fully read by readFile.
finding.source: A zip entry (for example xl/media/*) in an attacker-supplied xlsx with a declared uncompressed size near 16GB that deflate compresses to about 17MB.
finding.sink: readFile preallocation make([]byte, 0, Size) at lib.go:162 and io.Copy at lib.go:164; worksheets and shared strings above UnzipXMLSizeLimit spill to TmpDir via unzipToTemp (lib.go:95-111).

trace.note: checkFileSize compares declared size and cumulative total against UnzipSizeLimit
non-worksheet, non-sharedStrings parts go to readFile with no per-part streaming

finding.guards_checked: checkFileSize (lib.go:33-41) rejects negative sizes and totals above the limit using declared sizes. Go archive/zip stops reading at the declared size, so header lies cannot exceed it. Limit is documented and can be lowered by the caller, but the default allows OOM from a small upload.
